works.name: GQ-005 · Where the Field Is Moving

assemblies.name: SISO Agent Stack
assemblies.summary: The versioned composition that turns intent into coordinated, verifiable, and durable agent work across a project.
assemblies.outcome: A human can state an outcome, agents can execute it through persistent coordinated lanes, and a future agent can recover the verified project state without reconstructing chat.

responsibilities: Expose project architecture, canonical work, claims, run packets, verification, delivery, and durable knowledge.
Persist the state that lets a cold agent resume work without relying on chat or terminal history.

evidence.summary: Project OS README, specification, capability guide, and work lifecycle were read before assigning this assembly role.

components.role: local agent launcher and runtime surface
responsibilities: Launch the coding-agent runtime used by the stack.
Supply the shared status, routing, context, lifecycle, and capability surfaces installed for agents.

evidence.summary: Agent Base README was read directly; it describes a launcher and runtime surface rather than a generic agent framework.

components.role: persistent terminal workspace and lane substrate
responsibilities: Provide workspaces, tabs, panes, durable agent addressing, messaging, and observable persistent lanes.
Host the terminal processes through which the stack coordinates long-running agent work.

evidence.summary: The Herdr skill and its live operating laws were read directly; Herdr supplies mechanics, not a separate SISO control-plane category.

responsibilities: Hold user intent, priorities, lane boundaries, durable context, and final synthesis.
Resolve and coordinate the real workers in Herdr while distinguishing dispatch, worker report, and independent verification.

evidence.summary: The current Agent Zero skill was read directly; it defines a coordination layer and Herdr protocol, not a standalone playbook shelf.

operating_loop.action: Interpret the human outcome against the project's canonical state and constraints.
operating_loop.output: A bounded objective with current facts, ownership, and proof requirements.

operating_loop.action: Choose and brief the appropriate agent capability and execution lane.
operating_loop.output: An explicit work packet and return contract.

operating_loop.action: Run and observe the agent in an addressable terminal lane.
operating_loop.output: Worker artifacts, status, and a returned verdict.

operating_loop.action: Record claims, attempts, independent verification, delivery evidence, and durable learning.
operating_loop.output: Recoverable project truth rather than terminal-only history.

operating_loop.action: Synthesize verified state for the human and select the next bounded action.
operating_loop.output: A closed loop from intent to evidence-backed result.

capability_model.skill: A reusable agent capability with a trigger, bounded instructions, and an expected result contract.
capability_model.playbook: A scenario-specific composition that selects and sequences skills, tools, lanes, evidence, and verification; it may itself be delivered through a skill.
capability_model.placement_rule: Skills and playbooks stay with the component or package that owns their behavior and are indexed across the stack; they are not separate top-level stack layers.

evidence.summary: Assembly derived from direct reading of the current Project OS, Agent Base, Herdr, Agent Zero, orchestration-playbook, and SISO Agent Playbook sources.

assemblies.name: SISO Agent Stack
assemblies.summary: The expanded, publicly distributable composition of project operating state, provider-neutral runtime, coordination, capabilities, playbooks, lifecycle hooks, optional shared state and learning, integrations, and persistent terminal lanes.
assemblies.outcome: A new operator can clone one public distribution, install exact component revisions into an isolated Claude Code and Codex profile, verify every managed surface, and still address, fork, update, or omit each component independently.

responsibilities: Expose architecture, canonical work, claims, verification, delivery, and cold-pickup state.
Keep project truth in the project rather than in the portable global profile.

evidence.summary: Project OS is a required independently pinned component of the public distribution.

responsibilities: Run agent sessions, lifecycle, context, status, profiles, and command surfaces.
Remain replaceable independently from coordination policy and project state.

evidence.summary: Runtime is required and pinned independently from Agent Zero, Brain, and integrations.

responsibilities: Hold current intent, priorities, lane boundaries, and synthesis policy.
Build explicit worker packets and distinguish dispatch, worker report, and independent verification.

evidence.summary: Agent Zero is required and exact-pinned as the coordination layer.

responsibilities: Supply reusable capabilities with bounded instructions and expected results.
Install the same reviewed capability sources into both supported hosts.

evidence.summary: The installer discovered and linked 32 exact skill sources into Claude Code and Codex.

responsibilities: Compose skills, tools, prompts, lanes, evidence, and verification for repeatable scenarios.
Provide worker and lane commands without absorbing the Skills registry.

evidence.summary: Playbook is a required exact-pinned package and remains independently addressable.

components.role: host lifecycle automation and mechanical guardrails
responsibilities: Generate host-native lifecycle configuration from one versioned manifest.
Track privacy-reduced lifecycle state, guard narrow destructive commands, and require evidence after mutation.

evidence.summary: Seven hooks, both profiles, exact doctor checks, 21 tests, and 97/100 adversarial review passed.

responsibilities: Provide tasks, artifacts, memory, timeline, heartbeat, cost, and coordination APIs when shared durable state is needed.
Keep runtime databases and personal state outside the public distribution source.

evidence.summary: Brain is optional, exact-pinned, and installed as source plus commands without copying live databases.

responsibilities: Learn from explicitly supplied sessions using privacy-reduced records.
Retain an independent lifecycle because raw session inputs and learned state are not distribution source.

evidence.summary: Session Intelligence is optional and exact-pinned; no raw sessions are bundled.

responsibilities: Provide opt-in adapters around the runtime.
Preserve promotion, rollback, and source boundaries independently from runtime core.

evidence.summary: Integrations is optional, source-only, exact-pinned, and included in full non-external verification.

responsibilities: Provide addressable workspaces, tabs, panes, messaging, and durable terminal lanes.
Remain externally owned, separately licensed, and separately installed.

evidence.summary: External Apache-2.0 source is optional and pinned without changing ownership.

operating_loop.action: Interpret the requested outcome against project truth and the portable operating profile.
operating_loop.output: A bounded objective, constraints, ownership, and proof contract.

operating_loop.action: Select host-native agent roles, atomic capabilities, scenario tooling, and execution lanes.
operating_loop.output: Explicit worker packets and a version-resolved execution plan.

operating_loop.action: Run work through the selected host while lifecycle hooks and optional persistent lanes expose observable state.
operating_loop.output: Worker artifacts, lifecycle state, and returned verdicts.

operating_loop.action: Verify mutations, reject incomplete or dirty state, and persist only the appropriate project or optional shared-state records.
operating_loop.output: Evidence-backed, recoverable state without publishing private runtime data.

operating_loop.action: Synthesize the verified outcome and selectively use optional learning or adapters under their own boundaries.
operating_loop.output: A human-facing result and the next bounded action.

capability_model.skill: A reusable host-discoverable capability with a trigger, bounded instructions, and an expected result contract.
capability_model.playbook: A scenario-specific composition that sequences skills, tools, agents, lanes, evidence, and verification without absorbing their source identities.
capability_model.placement_rule: Every capability, hook, adapter, state service, and distribution stays with the Work that owns its behavior and release cadence; the Assembly records composition rather than filesystem containment.

evidence.summary: Assembly roles match the exact public distribution manifest, clean install receipts, explicit exclusions, and independent 97/100 and 98/100 reviews.
V2 expands rather than rewrites immutable V1, and separates the distribution bundle Work from the component Assembly it installs.

source_scopes.name: SISO workspace standards and operating maps

campaign.objective: Continuously turn evidenced local agent mechanisms into owned, sanitized, verified, released, Library-indexed, and stack-pinned capabilities without importing private state.

preservation.reason: The campaign records publication-safe findings only. It does not publish machine dirty state, mutate source roots, copy private configuration, or authorize cleanup.

units.name: Hooks registry and promotion governance

promotion.next_gate: Reconcile the legacy registry with the public manifest and add machine-verifiable maturity, portability, test, and latency fields.
blockers: The historical staging lifecycle was documented but never implemented.
Several registry entries describe specifications or machine-bound implementations rather than verified portable hooks.

units.rationale: The public Hooks Work distributes a curated baseline, while the older hub contains useful registry, audit, template, health, and promotion concepts that remain unproductized.

evidence.summary: The hub design, README, audit contract, registry, and public Hooks manifest were read and compared.

units.name: Manifest-driven deterministic policy guards
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks optional policy pack

promotion.next_gate: Separate generic destructive-action, authority, and repository-safety rules from personal routing policy and add false-positive fixtures.
blockers: The source combines portable safeguards with operator-specific model and path policy.

units.rationale: The local guard enforces a broader collection of prevention rules than the released safety hook, but its policy and host adapter are not yet separated.

evidence.summary: The hook implementation and the released safety-guard behavior were read and compared by policy responsibility.

units.name: Dispatch evidence contract hook

promotion.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral worker result schema and test numeric, existence, directional, and classification claims against required evidence.
blockers: The current parser is coupled to one host transcript format.

units.rationale: The Playbook describes evidence-backed worker returns, but stack recipients do not receive the local mechanism that checks those claims.

evidence.summary: The evidence hook and related Playbook dispatch contract were read and their distribution gap confirmed.

units.name: Closeout, earned-ask, and salvage gates
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks completion profile and Project OS reconciliation probe

promotion.next_gate: Extract a conservative policy core, define host adapters, and build precision and recall fixtures for completion and operator-attention decisions.
blockers: Transcript parsing and worktree discovery contain host and fleet assumptions.
Aggressive stop gates require false-positive measurement before default installation.

units.rationale: The local completion system covers unfinished work, unsupported done claims, unnecessary hand-backs, and stranded peer work beyond the released mutation-verification hook.

evidence.summary: Three local gate implementations and the portable verify-stop hook were read and compared.

units.name: Batching and delegation efficiency hooks
units.target: Optional SISO Agent Hooks efficiency profile

promotion.next_gate: Make thresholds configurable, reduce counters to publication-safe aggregates, and discover structured-search capability dynamically.
blockers: Current thresholds and indexed-project knowledge reflect one operator environment.

units.rationale: These hooks mechanically reinforce batching, bounded delegation, and structured code navigation that currently exist mostly as written operating guidance.

evidence.summary: The local hook behavior and overlapping fan-out and Playbook guidance were compared.

units.name: Warehouse-to-Hub skill reconciliation

promotion.next_gate: Read and classify every catalog delta, promote only current portable mechanisms, repair metadata, and record explicit retirement or Playbook ownership for the rest.
blockers: Name-level comparison is only a nomination signal.
Sampled entries include retired, malformed, nested, private, and scenario-sized material.

units.rationale: The warehouse contains substantially more skill documents than the released catalog, and a filtered audit found many names absent from both Skills and Playbook without proving that every delta should ship.

evidence.summary: Skill manifests were enumerated across the warehouse, Agent OS, released Skills registry, and released Playbook, followed by direct reads of priority candidates.

units.name: Priority portable skill batch

promotion.next_gate: Repair discovery metadata, preserve attribution, add trigger and negative tests, and verify bundled scripts with content-neutral fixtures.
blockers: Two candidates have incomplete or malformed discovery metadata.
The video skill requires fixture-based script verification before publication.

units.rationale: Direct review found a small high-value batch spanning fact verification, scope control, falsifiable investigation, volatile-state reminders, and video analysis.

evidence.summary: The selected skill bodies and their released-catalog absence were reviewed; portability gates remain open.

units.name: Pi Harness Lab
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime incubation or an independently evidenced Harness Lab Work

promotion.next_gate: Run parity analysis against released Runtime packages and identify code, tests, and research that remain uniquely useful.
blockers: The lab combines provider-specific experiments, generated patches, live verification, and functionality partly promoted elsewhere.
Independent adoption has not been established.

units.rationale: The lab has real packages and extensive local and live smoke surfaces for routing, lazy skills, child agents, councils, workflows, dashboards, lifecycle restore, and token budgets.

evidence.summary: The lab mission, package manifest, workspaces, agent profiles, experiments, and verification commands were read.

units.name: Provider-neutral child-task lifecycle

promotion.next_gate: Implement the typed state machine and an exactly-once notification regression fixture in Runtime control core.
blockers: The mechanism currently exists as a specification rather than released Runtime code.

units.rationale: The specification separates liveness, terminal result, output, and usage while requiring terminal-before-embellishment ordering and exactly-once parent notification.

evidence.summary: The lifecycle specification was read and exact contract names were checked against the released Runtime surface.

units.name: SISO TUI application and adapter parity
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime TUI packages and optional host adapters

promotion.next_gate: Extract renderer-neutral components and status adapters, then measure the remaining provider-specific application boundary.
blockers: The released Runtime intentionally contains contracts rather than raw application and renderer parity.
Pi-native patches require an optional adapter boundary.

units.rationale: The active terminal application contains renderer contracts, layouts, runtime and status adapters, and interaction code beyond the currently released TUI contracts package.

evidence.summary: The TUI README, package surfaces, application boundary, and existing Runtime extraction record were reconciled.

units.name: Agent-legible repository standards
units.target: SISO Project OS standards and verifier package

promotion.next_gate: Reconcile overlapping rules, separate portable templates from workspace examples, and add cold-agent orientation and structure conformance checks.
blockers: The source combines general standards with historical workspace-specific examples and personal paths.

units.rationale: The sources define a useful cold-agent orientation test, boot placement, depth and naming rules, universal agent primitives, ADR governance, structural ratchets, and handoff contracts.

evidence.summary: The conventions, standards index, architecture skill, enforcement templates, and module handoff format were read.

units.name: Manager–Worker–Validator artifact improvement playbook

promotion.next_gate: Package role prompts, file-handoff schemas, exactly-one-change enforcement, retry bounds, and an unintended-change fixture.
blockers: The current mechanism is warehouse documentation rather than an installable verified scenario.

units.rationale: The triad offers a disciplined reusable loop: analysis-only manager, exactly-one-change worker, and binary validator with unintended-change auto-failure.

evidence.summary: The three role contracts and the evidence-backed prompting principles were read and compared with released Playbook scenarios.

units.name: Agent Stack benchmark and proof harness
units.target: Runtime evaluation packages and Agent Stack release proof

promotion.next_gate: Sanitize cases, define a stable scorecard schema, and make clean-install, routing, lifecycle, fault, privacy, and recovery checks release evidence for the whole stack.
blockers: Some existing cases and reports encode retired hosts, private routing, or historical environment facts.

units.rationale: The harness already models task success, efficiency, code navigation, delegation, durability, verification, coordination, skills, safety, memory, fault injection, and soak tiers.

evidence.summary: The benchmark plan, task families, scorecard, representative results, and mechanism-level evaluation brief were read.

units.name: Agent Zero replay-only voice contracts
units.target: SISO Agent Zero optional voice adapter

promotion.next_gate: Promote typed intent, binding, receipt, handoff, risk, idempotency, and replay fixtures while retaining dry-run-only transport.
blockers: Live dispatch remains intentionally gated.
Current target discovery and lane admission include operator environment assumptions.

units.rationale: The extension contains a safer typed and fail-closed interface that the released Agent Zero Work currently records only as deferred capability.

evidence.summary: Typed contracts, risk tiers, idempotency, replay fixtures, and the released Agent Zero boundary were read and compared.

units.name: Atlas read-only architectural auditor
units.target: SISO Agent Integrations initially; independent Atlas Work only after activity proof

promotion.next_gate: Prove a live consumer and activity history, then sanitize the rubric and dependency surface before incubation.
blockers: Operational usage remains unverified.
The rubric includes personal and business-specific criteria.

units.rationale: Atlas defines a distinct graph-assisted, read-only investigation loop with three-critic triangulation, deduplication, and ticket emission only after agreement.

evidence.summary: The README, rubric, scripts, source map, and ticket-only boundary were read; activity was not inferred.

units.name: Cross-host agent operator HUD

promotion.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral status input contract and capability-detected Claude and Codex render adapters.
blockers: The existing statusline consumes one host's transcript and rate-limit surfaces.

units.rationale: The dependency-free statusline provides model, context pressure, token flow, reset, rate-limit, and session-cost feedback missing from the portable stack.

evidence.summary: The statusline implementation and existing portable agent-state hook were read and compared.

units.name: Memory lifecycle hook adapter
units.target: SISO Agent Brain or Session Intelligence optional lifecycle integration

promotion.next_gate: Model lifecycle events without personal memory payloads and run a privacy threat review before any extraction.
blockers: The current capability is coupled to plugin-local memory and host lifecycle events.
No personal memory content may enter the public source or fixtures.

units.rationale: The lifecycle configuration suggests reusable SessionStart, PostToolUse, and Stop integration, but only the event contract is eligible for public review.

evidence.summary: Only the hook lifecycle contract was reviewed; private memory payloads, databases, logs, and personal state were excluded.

units.name: Generated workspace ownership and domain canon
units.target: SISO Project OS drift checks and Great Library operating docs

promotion.next_gate: Generate human summaries from the domain manifest and fail verification when declared repository counts or ownership boundaries drift.
blockers: Current root documents are hand-maintained and disagree with the expanded ten-repository Agents domain.

units.rationale: The live domain manifest records the current estate, while root orientation and ownership documents still contain older repository counts and incomplete boundaries.

evidence.summary: The root orientation documents, ownership map, and current Agents domain manifest were read and compared.

Three bounded read-only discovery lanes reviewed publication-safe mechanisms across agent host configuration, the Agent Base warehouse, Agent OS, and workspace standards; every recorded unit has content-based evidence and a named next gate.
The campaign is a promotion queue, not a release claim. Private state, credentials, client source, sessions, logs, databases, telemetry, and personal memory payloads are excluded.

evidence.summary: Runtime release, manifest, behavior tests, architecture, migration map, and publication safety gate passed.

units.name: Agent session lifecycle

evidence.summary: The exported TypeScript contract and runtime event surface were read directly.

evidence.summary: The exported compact-packet types, store surface, distillation export, and host hooks were read directly.

units.name: Agent status and evidence surface

evidence.summary: The extension API, UI hooks, commands, tool contract, and custom message surface were read directly.

units.rationale: The release publishes normalized runtime/UI event contracts. The raw OpenTUI application, renderer adapters, and provider session host remain deferred until a later audited release.

units.name: Atlas architectural auditor

evidence.summary: Lab mission, target architecture, workspaces, experiments, and verification package were read directly.

evidence.summary: The sidecar boundary, lossless rules, launch harness, Oracle contract, live canary, rollback, and non-promotion decision were read directly.

units.name: Knowledge distillation engine

evidence.summary: The architecture, live stages, planned stages, data model, runner model, current corpus scale, and sibling-engine relationship were read directly.

units.name: Coding principles evidence engine
units.rationale: The public Principles Engine now retains source tiers, independent corroboration, adversarial gates, jury votes, deterministic scores, and canonical promotion without the product-name ambiguity or private corpus coupling.

evidence.summary: The harvest-to-render pipeline, credibility tiers, evidence gates, database migration, corpus boundary, and promotion logic were read directly.

units.name: Evidence-gated idea engine
units.rationale: The public Idea Engine now maintains evidence gates, groundedness, novelty, layer and gameability review, deterministic ROI-effort-risk ranking, and queued state. Autonomous code mutation and machine scheduling were excluded as separate authority boundaries.

evidence.summary: The propose-rate-render pipeline, gates, lifecycle, database dependency, and planning-front-door composition were read directly.

units.name: Agent session intelligence

units.name: Agent brain service

evidence.summary: The daemon contract, HTTP service, SQLite ownership, auth tiers, CLI client, degraded outbox, doctor checks, and machine-specific configuration were read directly.

units.name: Shared design system
units.target: Shared SISO product and UI ownership after a preservation bridge
units.rationale: The component bank, viewer, CLI, and MCP package serve multiple products and do not implement knowledge production; extensive dirty work blocks an immediate move.

evidence.summary: The nested repository role, remote, and dirty state were directly verified.

units.name: Historical source awaiting evidence-led promotion
units.target: Provenance-preserving source inventories, not canonical corpus
units.rationale: Historical source may contain valuable material but must retain origin, rights, and history until individual units pass promotion gates.

evidence.summary: The published boundary guide forbids treating inventories as canonical knowledge by default.
The public boundary release preserves the mixed local checkout while publishing only reviewed structure, policies, and receipts.
Moved legacy units, retired compatibility naming, preserved archive destinations, and deliberate boundary exceptions are recorded.

campaigns.objective: Continuously turn evidenced local agent mechanisms into owned, sanitized, verified, released, Library-indexed, and stack-pinned capabilities without importing private state.

units.name: Hooks registry and promotion governance
units.next_gate: Reconcile the legacy registry with the public manifest and add machine-verifiable maturity, portability, test, and latency fields.
blockers: The historical staging lifecycle was documented but never implemented.
Several registry entries describe specifications or machine-bound implementations rather than verified portable hooks.
units.rationale: The public Hooks Work distributes a curated baseline, while the older hub contains useful registry, audit, template, health, and promotion concepts that remain unproductized.

evidence.summary: The hub design, README, audit contract, registry, and public Hooks manifest were read and compared.

units.name: Manifest-driven deterministic policy guards
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks optional policy pack
units.next_gate: Separate generic destructive-action, authority, and repository-safety rules from personal routing policy and add false-positive fixtures.
blockers: The source combines portable safeguards with operator-specific model and path policy.
units.rationale: The local guard enforces a broader collection of prevention rules than the released safety hook, but its policy and host adapter are not yet separated.

evidence.summary: The hook implementation and the released safety-guard behavior were read and compared by policy responsibility.

units.name: Dispatch evidence contract hook
units.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral worker result schema and test numeric, existence, directional, and classification claims against required evidence.
blockers: The current parser is coupled to one host transcript format.
units.rationale: The Playbook describes evidence-backed worker returns, but stack recipients do not receive the local mechanism that checks those claims.

evidence.summary: The evidence hook and related Playbook dispatch contract were read and their distribution gap confirmed.

units.name: Closeout, earned-ask, and salvage gates
units.target: SISO Agent Hooks completion profile and Project OS reconciliation probe
units.next_gate: Extract a conservative policy core, define host adapters, and build precision and recall fixtures for completion and operator-attention decisions.
blockers: Transcript parsing and worktree discovery contain host and fleet assumptions.
Aggressive stop gates require false-positive measurement before default installation.
units.rationale: The local completion system covers unfinished work, unsupported done claims, unnecessary hand-backs, and stranded peer work beyond the released mutation-verification hook.

evidence.summary: Three local gate implementations and the portable verify-stop hook were read and compared.

units.name: Batching and delegation efficiency hooks
units.target: Optional SISO Agent Hooks efficiency profile
units.next_gate: Make thresholds configurable, reduce counters to publication-safe aggregates, and discover structured-search capability dynamically.
blockers: Current thresholds and indexed-project knowledge reflect one operator environment.
units.rationale: These hooks mechanically reinforce batching, bounded delegation, and structured code navigation that currently exist mostly as written operating guidance.

evidence.summary: The local hook behavior and overlapping fan-out and Playbook guidance were compared.

units.name: Warehouse-to-Hub skill reconciliation
units.next_gate: Read and classify every catalog delta, promote only current portable mechanisms, repair metadata, and record explicit retirement or Playbook ownership for the rest.
blockers: Name-level comparison is only a nomination signal.
Sampled entries include retired, malformed, nested, private, and scenario-sized material.
units.rationale: The warehouse contains substantially more skill documents than the released catalog, and a filtered audit found many names absent from both Skills and Playbook without proving that every delta should ship.

evidence.summary: Skill manifests were enumerated across the warehouse, Agent OS, released Skills registry, and released Playbook, followed by direct reads of priority candidates.

units.name: Priority portable skill batch
units.next_gate: Repair discovery metadata, preserve attribution, add trigger and negative tests, and verify bundled scripts with content-neutral fixtures.
blockers: Two candidates have incomplete or malformed discovery metadata.
The video skill requires fixture-based script verification before publication.
units.rationale: Direct review found a small high-value batch spanning fact verification, scope control, falsifiable investigation, volatile-state reminders, and video analysis.

evidence.summary: The selected skill bodies and their released-catalog absence were reviewed; portability gates remain open.

units.name: Pi Harness Lab
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime incubation or an independently evidenced Harness Lab Work
units.next_gate: Run parity analysis against released Runtime packages and identify code, tests, and research that remain uniquely useful.
blockers: The lab combines provider-specific experiments, generated patches, live verification, and functionality partly promoted elsewhere.
Independent adoption has not been established.
units.rationale: The lab has real packages and extensive local and live smoke surfaces for routing, lazy skills, child agents, councils, workflows, dashboards, lifecycle restore, and token budgets.

evidence.summary: The lab mission, package manifest, workspaces, agent profiles, experiments, and verification commands were read.

units.name: Provider-neutral child-task lifecycle
units.next_gate: Implement the typed state machine and an exactly-once notification regression fixture in Runtime control core.
blockers: The mechanism currently exists as a specification rather than released Runtime code.
units.rationale: The specification separates liveness, terminal result, output, and usage while requiring terminal-before-embellishment ordering and exactly-once parent notification.

evidence.summary: The lifecycle specification was read and exact contract names were checked against the released Runtime surface.

units.name: SISO TUI application and adapter parity
units.target: SISO Agent Runtime TUI packages and optional host adapters
units.next_gate: Extract renderer-neutral components and status adapters, then measure the remaining provider-specific application boundary.
blockers: The released Runtime intentionally contains contracts rather than raw application and renderer parity.
Pi-native patches require an optional adapter boundary.
units.rationale: The active terminal application contains renderer contracts, layouts, runtime and status adapters, and interaction code beyond the currently released TUI contracts package.

evidence.summary: The TUI README, package surfaces, application boundary, and existing Runtime extraction record were reconciled.

units.name: Agent-legible repository standards
units.target: SISO Project OS standards and verifier package
units.next_gate: Reconcile overlapping rules, separate portable templates from workspace examples, and add cold-agent orientation and structure conformance checks.
blockers: The source combines general standards with historical workspace-specific examples and personal paths.
units.rationale: The sources define a useful cold-agent orientation test, boot placement, depth and naming rules, universal agent primitives, ADR governance, structural ratchets, and handoff contracts.

evidence.summary: The conventions, standards index, architecture skill, enforcement templates, and module handoff format were read.

units.name: Manager–Worker–Validator artifact improvement playbook
units.next_gate: Package role prompts, file-handoff schemas, exactly-one-change enforcement, retry bounds, and an unintended-change fixture.
blockers: The current mechanism is warehouse documentation rather than an installable verified scenario.
units.rationale: The triad offers a disciplined reusable loop: analysis-only manager, exactly-one-change worker, and binary validator with unintended-change auto-failure.

evidence.summary: The three role contracts and the evidence-backed prompting principles were read and compared with released Playbook scenarios.

units.name: Agent Stack benchmark and proof harness
units.target: Runtime evaluation packages and Agent Stack release proof
units.next_gate: Sanitize cases, define a stable scorecard schema, and make clean-install, routing, lifecycle, fault, privacy, and recovery checks release evidence for the whole stack.
blockers: Some existing cases and reports encode retired hosts, private routing, or historical environment facts.
units.rationale: The harness already models task success, efficiency, code navigation, delegation, durability, verification, coordination, skills, safety, memory, fault injection, and soak tiers.

evidence.summary: The benchmark plan, task families, scorecard, representative results, and mechanism-level evaluation brief were read.

units.name: Agent Zero replay-only voice contracts
units.target: SISO Agent Zero optional voice adapter
units.next_gate: Promote typed intent, binding, receipt, handoff, risk, idempotency, and replay fixtures while retaining dry-run-only transport.
blockers: Live dispatch remains intentionally gated.
Current target discovery and lane admission include operator environment assumptions.
units.rationale: The extension contains a safer typed and fail-closed interface that the released Agent Zero Work currently records only as deferred capability.

evidence.summary: Typed contracts, risk tiers, idempotency, replay fixtures, and the released Agent Zero boundary were read and compared.

units.name: Atlas read-only architectural auditor
units.target: SISO Agent Integrations initially; independent Atlas Work only after activity proof
units.next_gate: Prove a live consumer and activity history, then sanitize the rubric and dependency surface before incubation.
blockers: Operational usage remains unverified.
The rubric includes personal and business-specific criteria.
units.rationale: Atlas defines a distinct graph-assisted, read-only investigation loop with three-critic triangulation, deduplication, and ticket emission only after agreement.

evidence.summary: The README, rubric, scripts, source map, and ticket-only boundary were read; activity was not inferred.

units.name: Cross-host agent operator HUD
units.next_gate: Define a provider-neutral status input contract and capability-detected Claude and Codex render adapters.
blockers: The existing statusline consumes one host's transcript and rate-limit surfaces.
units.rationale: The dependency-free statusline provides model, context pressure, token flow, reset, rate-limit, and session-cost feedback missing from the portable stack.

evidence.summary: The statusline implementation and existing portable agent-state hook were read and compared.

units.name: Memory lifecycle hook adapter
units.target: SISO Agent Brain or Session Intelligence optional lifecycle integration
units.next_gate: Model lifecycle events without personal memory payloads and run a privacy threat review before any extraction.
blockers: The current capability is coupled to plugin-local memory and host lifecycle events.
No personal memory content may enter the public source or fixtures.
units.rationale: The lifecycle configuration suggests reusable SessionStart, PostToolUse, and Stop integration, but only the event contract is eligible for public review.

evidence.summary: Only the hook lifecycle contract was reviewed; private memory payloads, databases, logs, and personal state were excluded.

units.name: Generated workspace ownership and domain canon
units.target: SISO Project OS drift checks and Great Library operating docs
units.next_gate: Generate human summaries from the domain manifest and fail verification when declared repository counts or ownership boundaries drift.
blockers: Current root documents are hand-maintained and disagree with the expanded ten-repository Agents domain.
units.rationale: The live domain manifest records the current estate, while root orientation and ownership documents still contain older repository counts and incomplete boundaries.

evidence.summary: The root orientation documents, ownership map, and current Agents domain manifest were read and compared.
